steps.title: See it
steps.text: The biskni moves like a bishop but takes like a knight. It slides along a diagonal to an empty square, as far as it likes, and it captures with a knight's jump. It can't take along its diagonals, and it can't jump to an empty square. Its name joins bishop and knight, the other way round from the knibis. The dots mark where it can move, and the rings mark where it could take an enemy piece.

steps.title: Try it
steps.text: Slide to e5 along the diagonal, then take the black knight on g6 with a knight's jump.

pages.text: The biskni crosses the board like a bishop, but strikes only close by, with a knight's jump. Unlike a bishop, it lands on the other colour each time it takes. Here it can take the rook on c6, or slide all the way to h8.

It gives check only with a knight's jump, so first it slides to a square a jump away from the king. Here it slides to g6 and checks the king on h8 from there. Your king and other pieces must cover the squares around the king that the biskni leaves open.
It can't take along its diagonals, so a bishop can attack it and not be taken back. Here the black bishop on g7 attacks it. The biskni slides away, here to b6, off the bishop's diagonal.

puzzles.hint: The biskni takes like a knight.

puzzles.prompt: Win the black pawn in two moves.
puzzles.hint: Slide to a square from which a knight's jump checks the king and another would take the pawn.
Slide to a square a knight's jump from the king. Your king and your other biskni cover the rest.
The king has no moves at all. A check from b6 would fail, as the pawn could take. Find a square from which the biskni can slide next move into a check that nothing can take.
